tasks.objective: Bound the polling feed in src/adapter/useCanvas.ts (finding 6acbe3a3, epic criterion 1): at most one overview+timelines request set may be outstanding at any moment. A setInterval tick that fires while load() is still in flight starts nothing new (it is skipped, or at most folded into the single trailing load described next); a refresh() — the forced tick every write fires through source.onWrote() — that arrives while a load is in flight is coalesced into exactly one trailing load() that starts when the in-flight one settles, so a write's effect still shows up once instead of stacking one request set per call. The guard is released on success AND on failure, so a rejected load never stalls polling. Keep the existing alive/generation guards, POLL_MS, the exported CanvasFeed shape, useCanvas's signature and the App.tsx call site unchanged. Add tests to test/adapter/useCanvas.test.tsx that fail against HEAD d42cfc0 and pass against the fix, using the file's existing fake-timer + act pattern.

Hypothesis (fixed): overview was called exactly 1 time. Null (HEAD d42cfc0, one load per tick regardless): the same assertion fails with `expected 4 to be 1` (the mount-time load plus one per tick).

C2 — refresh() coalesces instead of stacking. Hypothesis: overview was called exactly 2 times (the held one plus exactly one trailing load) and status ends 'live'; a further `await act(async () => {})` with no timer advance leaves the count at 2 (a coalescer that re-arms itself would push it to 3).
